Definition: Average CPU utilisation across all hosts in each vSphere cluster as a % of total available CPU capacity. High utilisation risks performance degradation and reduces headroom for HA failover.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No capacity monitoring. CPU utilisation unknown. VMs frequently competing for resources.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic monitoring in place. Average utilisation often above 80%. No capacity planning.
Level 3 - Defined: CPU utilisation tracked. Average between 60-80%. Alerts configured. Quarterly capacity review.
Level 4 - Managed: Average CPU below 70%. DRS automation balanced across hosts. Proactive capacity planning.
Level 5 - Optimized: Average CPU below 60%. Predictive capacity management. DRS fully automated. Zero resource contention incidents.

Definition: The ratio of virtual CPUs allocated to VMs versus physical CPU cores available per cluster. Over-subscription impacts performance under load.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Ratio unknown. No governance on VM sizing. Significant over-commitment present.
Level 2 - Developing: Ratio tracked per cluster but frequently exceeds 8:1. Performance issues common under load.
Level 3 - Defined: Ratio maintained at or below 6:1 for most clusters. VM sizing guidelines exist.
Level 4 - Managed: Ratio at or below 4:1 for production clusters. Right-sizing reviews conducted. Alerts on breach.
Level 5 - Optimized: Ratio at or below 3:1 for critical workloads. Automated right-sizing recommendations. VM sizing enforced via policy.

Parameter / KPI: Memory Balloon and Swap Activity Rate
Definition: Frequency and magnitude of VMware memory reclamation techniques being invoked, indicating memory pressure across the cluster.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Memory pressure events frequent. No monitoring. VMs experience significant performance degradation.
Level 2 - Developing: Ballooning events occur regularly. Monitored reactively. No proactive response.
Level 3 - Defined: Ballooning events tracked and alerted. Proactive memory additions when thresholds are breached.
Level 4 - Managed: Ballooning rare, fewer than 5 events per month per cluster. Memory headroom maintained. Automated alerts.
Level 5 - Optimized: Zero ballooning or swap events. Predictive memory management. Resource pools enforce isolation.

Definition: Average read and write latency experienced by VMs, measured at the datastore or vSAN level. Targets are read below 10ms and write below 5ms for production workloads.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Storage latency not monitored. Performance issues reported by end users. No baseline established.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic latency monitoring. Latency often exceeds 20ms. No SLA defined. Reactive response only.
Level 3 - Defined: Latency monitored per datastore. SLA defined. Average read below 15ms, write below 10ms.
Level 4 - Managed: Latency consistently at read below 10ms and write below 5ms. Alerts trigger capacity review.
Level 5 - Optimized: Read below 5ms, write below 2ms. Predictive I/O analytics. Automated tiering. Zero latency incidents.

Definition: % of vSphere clusters with HA Admission Control enabled and configured to reserve sufficient resources to tolerate at least one host failure without violating VM restart guarantees.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: HA not configured or disabled on most clusters. Single points of failure unmanaged.
Level 2 - Developing: HA enabled but Admission Control not configured. No guarantee of failover capacity.
Level 3 - Defined: HA with Admission Control enabled on all production clusters. Tolerance set for 1 host failure.
Level 4 - Managed: HA and Admission Control configured for N+1 or N+2 tolerance. Tested annually. Alerts on policy drift.
Level 5 - Optimized: HA tested quarterly via simulated host failures. N+2 for critical clusters. Automated compliance validation.

Definition: Tracking of VM snapshots older than 72 hours, which risk delta disk growth, performance degradation, and excessive storage consumption.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Snapshots created with no lifecycle policy. Snapshots weeks or months old are common.
Level 2 - Developing: Snapshot age not routinely monitored. Ad hoc cleanup. Snapshots frequently exceed 7 days.
Level 3 - Defined: Snapshot report generated weekly. Snapshots exceeding 72 hours are flagged. Manual cleanup process.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated alerts on snapshots exceeding 24 hours. Auto-delete policy for snapshots over 72 hours in non-production.
Level 5 - Optimized: Zero snapshots older than 72 hours in production. Automated lifecycle management. Snapshot usage audited daily.

Parameter / KPI: RPO and RTO Compliance for Protected VMs
Definition: % of VMs covered by a defined backup or replication policy that meets the agreed Recovery Point Objective and Recovery Time Objective for their service tier.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No RPO or RTO defined for VMs. No protection policy. Recovery capability unknown.
Level 2 - Developing: RPO and RTO defined informally for some VMs. Coverage below 60%. Recovery never tested.
Level 3 - Defined: RPO and RTO defined for more than 75% of VMs by service tier. Backups monitored. Annual DR test.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 95% of VMs covered. SLA compliance reported monthly. DR tested twice yearly.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% of VMs covered. RPO and RTO validated continuously via automated recovery testing. Real-time SLA dashboard.

Definition: % of ESXi hosts running patch levels within the approved patching SLA, assessed against VMware published release cadence and security advisory bulletins.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: ESXi hosts rarely patched. Patch level unknown for most hosts. No formal process.
Level 2 - Developing: Patching occurs but inconsistently. Many hosts more than 6 months behind. No SLA defined.
Level 3 - Defined: Patch SLA defined. ESXi patched via Update Manager. More than 75% compliant.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 90% of ESXi hosts within patch SLA. Baseline profiles applied. Exceptions tracked.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% compliance. Lifecycle Manager automates ESXi updates. Patches tested in staging first.

Definition: Whether multi-factor authentication is enforced for all administrative access to vCenter Server and associated management interfaces via Identity Federation, Okta, or AD FS.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Single-factor password-only authentication for vCenter admin access.
Level 2 - Developing: MFA available but optional. Most administrators use password only. No enforcement.
Level 3 - Defined: MFA enforced for privileged and admin accounts. Standard monitoring accounts exempt.
Level 4 - Managed: MFA enforced for all accounts with write access. Identity federation configured.
Level 5 - Optimized: MFA enforced for all accounts including read-only. Phishing-resistant methods enforced. Privileged access via PAM vault.

Definition: % of VMs that are powered off for more than 30 days or are orphaned and not associated with an active workload, representing wasted resources and potential security risk.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No VM lifecycle management. Large number of powered-off and orphaned VMs. No tracking.
Level 2 - Developing: VM inventory exists but sprawl not tracked. More than 20% of VMs inactive. Cleanup ad hoc.
Level 3 - Defined: Sprawl report generated monthly. VMs powered off for more than 30 days are flagged. Cleanup process defined.
Level 4 - Managed: Sprawl tracked continuously. Less than 5% inactive VMs. Automated alerts trigger review workflow.
Level 5 - Optimized: Less than 2% inactive VMs. Automated decommission workflow. VM lifecycle fully governed.

Definition: % of capacity used across all datastores, with a target of maintaining below 80% to ensure performance and room for snapshot and temporary file growth.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Datastore utilisation not monitored. Full datastore events common. Reactive management.
Level 2 - Developing: Utilisation checked manually. Datastores frequently exceed 85%. No automated alerts.
Level 3 - Defined: Utilisation monitored with alerts at 80%. Monthly capacity review. Manual remediation.
Level 4 - Managed: Alerts at 75%. Automated capacity reporting. Storage provisioning triggered proactively.
Level 5 - Optimized: Utilisation maintained below 70%. Predictive analytics. Automated tiering and expansion. Zero datastore full events.

Definition: % of VMs running a current and supported version of VMware Tools, which is critical for performance and security guest OS visibility.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: VMware Tools not managed. Many VMs running outdated or missing Tools.
Level 2 - Developing: Tools version tracked but update process manual and infrequent. More than 30% outdated.
Level 3 - Defined: Tools updated during maintenance windows. More than 80% running supported versions.
Level 4 - Managed: More than 95% running current Tools. Automated update via vCenter policy. Exceptions tracked.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% current Tools. Automated update at VM power-on. Compliance enforced via policy.

Definition: % of vSphere infrastructure changes that complete successfully without causing unplanned outages or rollbacks.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal change process. Changes made ad hoc. Frequent outages caused by changes.
Level 2 - Developing: Change process defined but inconsistently followed. Success rate below 85%. Limited testing.
Level 3 - Defined: Change process followed for major changes. Success rate between 85-92%. Post-change reviews performed.
Level 4 - Managed: Success rate above 95%. Pre-change testing in non-production. Automated rollback for failures.
Level 5 - Optimized: More than 99% success rate. All changes follow automated pipeline. Pre and post validation automated.

Parameter / KPI: vMotion and Storage vMotion Success Rate & Performance
Definition: Metric definition: Percentage of vMotion and Storage vMotion operations that complete successfully without errors or manual intervention, combined with average migration duration and stun time. How measured: (Successful migrations / Total attempted migrations) x 100.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: <80% success rate. Frequent failures or timeouts; no dedicated vMotion network. Average duration >10 minutes.
Level 2 - Developing: 80-90% success rate. Basic vMotion network configured; average migration time 5-10 minutes.
Level 3 - Defined: 91-97% success rate. Dedicated vMotion vmkernel ports with at least 10 GbE; average vMotion duration <3 minutes.
Level 4 - Managed: 98-99.5% success rate. Multi-NIC vMotion with load balancing and jumbo frames; pre-flight checks in place.
Level 5 - Optimized: >=99.5% success rate with zero unplanned failures. Predictive scheduling and advanced techniques.

Definition: Metric definition: Percentage of ESXi hosts, Distributed Switches, and port groups that comply with standardized networking baselines, combined with network utilization, latency, and packet drop rates.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: <60% compliance. Frequent configuration drift; high utilization (>90%) or latency (>10 ms); packet drops common.
Level 2 - Developing: 60-80% compliance. Utilization often exceeds 80%; vMotion latency 5-10 ms; basic alerts configured.
Level 3 - Defined: 81-95% compliance. All production clusters use vDS; peak utilization <70%; vMotion latency <5 ms.
Level 4 - Managed: 96-99% compliance. Uniform vDS policies, jumbo frames, and QoS enforced; utilization <60%; latency <2 ms.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% compliance with zero drift. Utilization proactively managed; predictive analytics for congestion.

Parameter / KPI: Percentage of Routine Operational Tasks Automated
Definition: Metric definition: Percentage of recurring operational tasks (VM provisioning, patching, snapshot cleanup, compliance checks, reporting, resource reclamation) that are fully automated with no manual intervention required.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: <15% automated. Most tasks performed manually or with one-off scripts; no central process.
Level 2 - Developing: 15-40% automated. Basic PowerCLI or shell scripts used for some tasks; limited scheduling.
Level 3 - Defined: 41-70% automated. Standard scripts and workflows exist in a central repository; scheduled via vSphere Lifecycle Manager.
Level 4 - Managed: 71-90% automated. Policy-driven workflows using Aria Automation / Orchestrator; integrated with approval processes.
Level 5 - Optimized: >90% automated. Self-service catalog, event-driven automation, and predictive capabilities.

Parameter / KPI: Automation Success Rate and Tool Adoption
Definition: Metric definition: Combined measure of (a) success rate of automated workflows/changes and (b) percentage of operational workflows executed through formal orchestration tools (Aria Automation, vRealize Orchestrator, Ansible, Terraform).
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Success rate <75% and tool adoption <20%. Frequent manual interventions; orchestration rarely used.
Level 2 - Developing: Success rate 75-88% and tool adoption 20-45%. Basic retry logic; orchestration tool used sporadically.
Level 3 - Defined: Success rate 89-95% and tool adoption 46-70%. Standardized workflows with logging and rollback.
Level 4 - Managed: Success rate 96-99% and tool adoption 71-90%. Automated rollback, pre-flight validation, and governance policies.
Level 5 - Optimized: Success rate >=99% and tool adoption >90%. Predictive validation, full self-service integration with ITSM/CMDB.
